ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure are the two terminals of AC voltage u, with the upper terminal marked “+” and the lower terminal marked “-”. The middle branch is a series-connected inductor L and resistor R: inductor L is above, and resistor R is below. On the right side there are two voltmeters; V1 is connected across inductor L, with a reading of 10 V marked beside it; V2 is connected across resistor R, also with a reading of 10 V marked beside it. Reasoning: In a series R-L AC circuit, the voltage across the resistor is in phase with the current, and the voltage across the inductor leads the current by 90°, so the phase difference between the resistor voltage and the inductor voltage is 90°. The RMS value of the total voltage u is the phasor sum of the two, namely the hypotenuse of a right triangle: U = sqrt(10^2 + 10^2) = sqrt(200) ≈ 14.1 V.

method.method_draft: Let the series current RMS value be I. The diagram’s voltmeter readings give IR = 10 and IX_L = 10, so R = 10/I and X_L = 10/I. The source voltage is I sqrt(R^2 + X_L^2) = I sqrt((10/I)^2 + (10/I)^2) = sqrt(200) ≈ 14.1 V.
